standard.title: Strategies for liveability
standard.description: strategies used to enhance the liveability of a place, including for young people, the aged or those with disability, drawing on studies such as those from Australia or Europe
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have completed K05–K07 — they can explain factors influencing residential decisions, analyse service distribution and its liveability implications, and explain how cultural connectedness shapes belonging and place perceptions. This standard is the synthesis point of the liveability unit — applying all prior conceptual work to the evaluation of strategies that improve liveability for specific community groups.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain strategies used to enhance the liveability of a place for different groups in the community.

nodes.label: Identifying liveability enhancement strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify strategies implemented in Australia or Europe to improve the liveability of a place and explain what aspect of liveability each targets.
nodes.minimum_width: Students identify at least two liveability strategies from Australia or Europe and explain what liveability problem each addresses.
nodes.typical_width: Students identify strategies implemented in Australia or a country in Europe to improve liveability — including improving public spaces, walkability, transport connections, water disposal and recycling — explaining what each targets and considering applicability to their own locality.
wider: Research a specific European city known for liveability enhancement (e.g. Vienna, Copenhagen, Amsterdam) and analyse which strategies contribute to its high liveability ratings and whether they are transferable to Australian cities

Compare strategies targeting physical infrastructure (transport, public space) with strategies targeting social infrastructure (community programs, cultural facilities) — which approach has greater liveability impact and for whom?
Investigate strategies in Australian cities that have improved liveability for specific groups — e.g. 20-minute neighbourhood planning, age-friendly city programs, disability access audits
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot identify a range of strategy types will evaluate liveability improvement narrowly (defaulting to infrastructure). This limits the evaluation capacity needed in node 3, where assessing applicability requires understanding which strategies address which liveability dimensions.

response_modes.reason: Widening to European exemplars alongside Australian cases gives students a richer strategy repertoire and allows them to see liveability enhancement as a field of active planning practice rather than an abstract aspiration.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The European-Australian comparison is explicitly called for in the descriptor and provides genuine comparative geographical analysis. Students who engage with contrasting urban planning contexts develop transferable analytical skills for evaluating place-based strategies.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two distinct liveability enhancement strategies from Australia or Europe, naming the strategy and the liveability problem it addresses.
Explains what aspect of liveability (physical, social, environmental, access) each strategy targets.

nodes.label: Diverse community needs and strategy design
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop or describe a strategy to improve an aspect of liveability that takes into account the needs of diverse groups, including young people, the aged, people with disability, or Traditional Owners.
nodes.minimum_width: Students explain how at least one community group's specific needs have been or could be addressed by a liveability strategy.
nodes.typical_width: Students develop a strategy (or examine an existing one) to improve an aspect of liveability at the local scale, taking into account the needs of at least two diverse groups — including young people, elderly residents, people with disability, or Traditional Owners — and explaining how the strategy addresses group-specific needs.
wider: Develop a bilingual or culturally-responsive signage proposal for a local area in consultation with First Nations Australians or other cultural communities — examine what this signals about whose belonging is recognised

Design an inclusive public space that addresses the specific needs of young people, elderly residents and people with disability simultaneously — where do needs align and where do they create design tensions?
Research Universal Design principles and evaluate how well an existing local space meets them, proposing specific improvements

response_modes.reason: Designing for diverse groups requires students to adopt multiple perspectives simultaneously. Using fieldwork in a real local space makes the design challenge concrete and prevents abstract generalisation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The design task for diverse groups is one of the most generative activities in the liveability unit — it requires applied synthesis of K05–K07 understanding and direct engagement with community members. Students who conduct fieldwork here produce genuine geographical knowledge about their local area.
success_criteria: Identifies the specific liveability needs of at least two different community groups for a proposed or analysed strategy.
Explains how the strategy design addresses or should address those specific needs.

nodes.label: Evaluating strategy applicability
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate a liveability strategy using criteria and decide on its applicability to their own locality.
nodes.minimum_width: Students apply at least two evaluation criteria to a liveability strategy and reach a reasoned conclusion about its applicability.
nodes.typical_width: Students evaluate a strategy to improve liveability using criteria — such as effectiveness for target groups, feasibility in local context, cost, equity of benefit, and environmental impact — and decide on its applicability to their own locality with reasons.
wider: Evaluate the same strategy against different criteria applied by different stakeholders — e.g. a developer, a disability advocate, a Traditional Owner, a young person — examine how criterion selection reflects values and interests
Compare how a strategy designed for a European context would need to be modified for an Australian context — examine what contextual factors would require modification
Develop a ranked set of liveability priorities for the local area and evaluate two or more strategies against those priorities

response_modes.reason: Criteria-based evaluation requires students to apply criteria consistently and reach a defensible conclusion. Scaffolding the evaluation process — selecting criteria, applying them with evidence, weighing and concluding — prevents evaluations that are really descriptions with a tagged-on opinion.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Criteria-based evaluation of place strategies is a transferable geographical inquiry skill. Students who practise this rigorously develop analytical capacity applicable across the entire curriculum — and the insight that criteria selection reflects values is an important meta-geographical lesson.
success_criteria: Applies at least two named criteria to evaluate a liveability strategy, using evidence to support each assessment.
Reaches a reasoned conclusion about the strategy's applicability to a specific local context, explaining the reasons.

nodes.label: Integration: liveability strategies and diverse communities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students explain strategies used to enhance the liveability of a place for diverse community groups — integrating strategy identification, needs analysis and evaluation.
nodes.minimum_width: Students produce an analysis of a liveability strategy that identifies targeted groups, explains how the strategy addresses their needs, and evaluates its applicability.
nodes.typical_width: Students produce an integrated analysis of a liveability strategy that: identifies the place context, explains the diverse community needs being addressed, describes the strategy and how it targets those needs, evaluates its effectiveness and applicability to the local context, and draws on at least one Australian or European comparative example.
wider: Develop an original liveability improvement proposal for a specific local place — including community needs assessment, strategy design, criteria evaluation and applicability argument — drawing on K05–K08 content throughout

Compare two Australian cities' liveability enhancement approaches (e.g. Melbourne vs Brisbane, or a capital vs a regional city) and evaluate which approach better addresses the needs of the most disadvantaged community groups

response_modes.reason: K08 is the synthesis standard for the entire liveability unit. The integration node requires students to draw on all liveability concepts — measurement, distribution, cultural connectedness, diverse needs — in a single coherent analysis of a place-based strategy.

success_criteria: Produces an analysis of a liveability strategy that addresses community group needs, strategy design, and applicability evaluation.
Draws on at least two liveability concepts from K05–K07 in the analysis.
